RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SquareStart_L1: Set the board on a steady bench and mark its face side before measuring.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SquareStart_L2: Hook the tape on the same end each time so every mark shares one reference.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SquareStart_L3: Bring the square against the edge and carry the pencil line across the board.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SquareStart_L4: Clamp the work securely and keep the saw on the waste side of the line.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SquareStart_L5: Check both diagonals before fastening a frame; equal lengths help keep it square.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ShelfSunday_L1: Plan the shelf around its load and mark the supports before cutting lumber.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ShelfSunday_L2: Inspect each board for splits near the ends before choosing a fastening point.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ShelfSunday_L3: Drill a pilot hole close to the board end to reduce splitting when driving a screw.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ShelfSunday_L4: Use a level while attaching the brackets and verify the fixing surface is sound.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ShelfSunday_L5: Load the finished shelf gradually and watch the brackets for movement.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DrivewayChecks_L1: Park on level ground, stop the engine and let it cool before an inspection.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DrivewayChecks_L2: Read the dipstick after wiping it clean and reinserting it fully.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DrivewayChecks_L3: Inspect coolant hoses for cracks and keep the pressure cap closed while hot.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DrivewayChecks_L4: Compare cold tire pressures with the vehicle specification, including the spare.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DrivewayChecks_L5: Record fluid loss or unusual wear so the next inspection can reveal a pattern.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WheelRoutine_L1: Chock the wheels and identify the correct lifting point before raising the car.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WheelRoutine_L2: Loosen wheel nuts slightly while the tire still rests on the ground.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WheelRoutine_L3: Support the vehicle on proper stands; a jack alone is not a working support.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WheelRoutine_L4: Inspect the removed tire for cuts and uneven wear across the tread.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WheelRoutine_L5: Tighten wheel nuts in a crossing pattern to the specified torque, then recheck.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_Title: VHS: Community First Aid: First Minutes
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_L1: Check that the scene is safe before approaching an injured person.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_L2: Call for help and check responsiveness and normal breathing without delay.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_L3: Use clean gloves or a barrier when handling blood or an open wound.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_L4: Apply firm direct pressure to serious external bleeding with a clean dressing.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstMinutes_L5: Keep the person warm and watch for changes while waiting for qualified help.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_Title: VHS: Community First Aid: Clean Dressings
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_L1: Wash your hands and prepare clean materials before changing a dressing.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_L2: Rinse a minor dirty wound with clean water and avoid rubbing exposed tissue.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_L3: Cover the cleaned area with a sterile dressing without touching its wound side.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_L4: Secure the bandage without cutting circulation and check the fingers or toes.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_CleanDressings_L5: Seek medical help for spreading redness, worsening pain, fever or deep wounds.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DeadCircuit_L1: Identify the circuit and disconnect its supply before opening electrical equipment.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DeadCircuit_L2: Prevent anyone from restoring power while the work area remains open.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DeadCircuit_L3: Check the tester on a known source before and after testing for absence of voltage.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DeadCircuit_L4: Replace damaged insulation and use connectors rated for the wire and application.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_DeadCircuit_L5: Close covers and clear the work area before safely restoring the supply.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_Title: VHS: Bench Radio: Finding the Fault
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_L1: Unplug the radio and follow the service instructions before opening its case.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_L2: Sketch the wire connections before removing a part so reassembly has a reference.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_L3: Look for loose connections, scorched components and cracked solder joints.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_L4: Use the schematic to trace one section at a time instead of changing random parts.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BenchRadio_L5: Check component values and polarity before fitting an approved replacement.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WeldPrep_L1: Clear flammable materials and provide ventilation before setting up the welding area.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WeldPrep_L2: Wear suitable eye, face and skin protection before striking an arc.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WeldPrep_L3: Clean rust, paint and contamination from the joint using a suitable preparation method.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WeldPrep_L4: Fit the parts closely and clamp them so the joint cannot shift while tacking.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WeldPrep_L5: Practice the machine settings on matching scrap before welding the actual assembly.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_Title: VHS: Weld Shop: A Steady Bead
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_L1: Check the lead connections and select consumables suited to the metal and process.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_L2: Support your working arm so the torch angle stays consistent along the joint.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_L3: Watch the molten pool and maintain a steady travel speed rather than chasing the sparks.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_L4: Let the work cool safely before cleaning and inspecting the finished bead.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_SteadyBead_L5: Look for cracks, undercut and poor fusion; structural work needs qualified inspection.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ForgeMorning_L1: Organize the forge, water and clear walking space before heating the first stock.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ForgeMorning_L2: Choose tongs that grip the stock firmly and check the hammer handle for damage.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ForgeMorning_L3: Heat the working section evenly and keep watching its condition at the fire.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ForgeMorning_L4: Stand square to the anvil and use controlled blows rather than an oversized hammer.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_ForgeMorning_L5: Treat every piece near the forge as hot until its temperature is safely confirmed.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_Title: VHS: Forge Practice: Hook and Eye
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_L1: Mark the length needed for the hook and allow extra stock for the bend.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_L2: Draw out the end with overlapping blows and rotate the stock to keep its section even.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_L3: Work the bend around the anvil horn in small steps rather than forcing one sharp fold.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_L4: Reheat before the stock becomes too cold to shape without cracking.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_HookAndEye_L5: Check the cooled hook against the pattern and remove sharp burrs from its edges.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_Title: VHS: Masonry Corner: The First Course
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_L1: Start with a sound level base and mark the wall position before mixing mortar.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_L2: Dry lay the first course to plan joints and avoid an awkward final cut.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_L3: Mix only the mortar you can use within its working time and follow its proportions.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_L4: Set corner units carefully and stretch a line to guide the face of the course.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_FirstCourse_L5: Check each unit for level and alignment while the mortar can still be adjusted.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_Title: VHS: Masonry Corner: The Brick Rhythm
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_L1: Keep joint thickness consistent so each course reaches the planned height.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_L2: Stagger vertical joints according to the chosen bond rather than stacking seams.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_L3: Spread an even mortar bed and butter the end before placing the next brick.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_L4: Use the line as a guide without pushing it outward with the brick face.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_BrickRhythm_L5: Protect fresh work from drying too quickly, heavy rain and freezing conditions.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_MendBasket_L1: Wash the fabric and inspect the damaged area before choosing thread and a patch.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_MendBasket_L2: Trim loose threads without enlarging the tear and support thin fabric from beneath.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_MendBasket_L3: Choose a patch larger than the weak area so the stitches anchor in sound cloth.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_MendBasket_L4: Keep small stitches evenly spaced and avoid pulling the fabric into puckers.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_MendBasket_L5: Finish the thread securely on the inside and check that the repair can flex.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WorkingHem_L1: Try the garment on and mark the hem while it hangs naturally.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WorkingHem_L2: Measure the allowance consistently and press the fold before stitching.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WorkingHem_L3: Baste the folded edge first so slippery fabric cannot creep during the final seam.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WorkingHem_L4: Choose needle and thread to suit the fabric weight and test on a spare scrap.
RM_PassiveSkillsVHS_WorkingHem_L5: Use light tension for a hidden hem and inspect the outside for visible pulls.
